A decision tree for choosing the conductive path, with three outcomes: copper mesh in the stack, a surface path (epoxy-bonded copper strip or braid, copper tape, conductive paint, applied after cure), or no CF. critics.verdict:
The six drafts are mostly sound. Section and heading numbers match src/ apart from the retitles the register asks for. There are zero em dashes, and each draft has one revision bump with a correct header and history row, an Effective date of 2026-10-10 and the status wording 'Draft, pending Lead signature'. I grepped every UI label in app/*.js and the add-in, and all of them exist (including the full 'Board density, min (lb/ft³)', 'Sign without it', 'Season by station', 'ShopSabre slot 1/2', 'Mark these boards cut…', '+ Link a mold…', 'Change this hold…'). Every numbered figure I checked matches its TDS: Ure-Bond, XCR, IN2, US West 205/206/209 and Airtac 2. No number comes from a stand-in. The drafters' three challenges to the register hold up against the files: the AT30 FAST SDS is inside the combined IN2 file (v6.0, 2022-09-08), AT30 SLOW's H332 appears only in §16, and holdState() reads only steps[idx-1].

These must be fixed before promotion:
- CS-006 §6 leaves out IN2 resin's H360F ('may damage fertility').
- CS-003 §6 cuts Ure-Bond Part A's hazards down to H334 and H319, dropping H317, H351, H332, H335, H373 and H315.
- CS-008's AT30 FAST row is missing EUH071.
- CS-004's Title field still breaks R-IDX-04.
- CS-003 §7.3 step 15 sends wet-layup runs to a 'Glue mold stock' step that does not exist on them.

Simon's 2026-10-10 answers override the register in five places the drafts predate:
- CS-006 §7.8 states 'we do not degas' and needs rewriting as an optional step.
- The tacky tape is Airtech AT-200Y.
- Blanks are cut on a saw (the ShopSabre may be used).
- The mold ID goes on the glued stack.
- The PPE rows (R-003-02, R-004-02, R-006-03, R-008-04) become shall-where-stocked or should-plus-purchase-list.

Lower priority: CS-007's caution adds a leads' rule with no register row, and an app-fix row is needed for holdState. The rest are small label, source and style fixes.

The seven drafts are close, and I'd fix them before promotion rather than redraft. Every do / do (rule) row the drafters claim is in the text. No hold: Simon item was changed: R-001-17 and R-001-19 are untouched, §7.4 step 1 still starts at glue-up, and §7.7's last line is unchanged. Heading lists match src apart from the appended §7.5 (CS-000), §7.11 to §7.13 (CS-001), §7.5 (CS-002) and §7.5 to §7.7 (CS-013), plus the renames the register allows. Each standard has one revision bump, dated 2026-10-10, with the status wording unchanged. Every UI label I grepped exists in app/*.js. There are no em dashes in new prose; the remaining ones are history rows, the print.js literal and the kept INDEX H1.

What needs fixing:
- **A lint conflict about quick references.** CS-000 §4 and QR-Template say "one Checked against per parent standard", and the INDEX rows are written that way. Lint 10 needs every Parent entry to carry its own CS-0xx ID and its own Checked against, so several QR headers would fail when written.
- **CS-INDEX.** The quick-reference table mixes Parent and Covers in one cell. One claim is invented: that honeycomb skins follow CS-007.
- **CS-000 §7.2.** Step 2 says check_traceability already accepts the Under Revision / Draft pairing. It doesn't until R-OTH-05 lands. The steps also announce a revision before it is deployed.
- **CS-001.** The fabric label is said to print an expiry date, but fabric records have no expiry field. The class word is called "never printed", but storage labels print STORAGE. The new 5522 shall contradicts the overlaminated-paper fallback in §7.8 and §7.9.
- **CS-002.** Some UI labels are stale ("season timeline", "qualityChecks").
- **Register decisions.** Simon or Nick should rule on four calls the drafters made: R-002-07 (ME vs RE), the trimmed R-002-02, the narrower R-013-05 shall, and the switch to 5522 for the demould label pair.

STYLE §6 and R-OTH-02 ('one Checked against each') say the same. 'Per parent standard' allows 'CS-008 §5; §5.1' with one check, and lint 10 fails that.
